messages.subject: QMET in ectotherms
parts:
Hi Mike,

My apologies if it is a bit of a naive question, but I was just wondering where the 0.0056 factor came from to convert respiration rate (VO2=ml/hr) to heat produced? (ie; lines 93, 99, 107 in https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/src/MET.f )

I couldn't find any direct mention of it in Kearney et al. (2020), Gates (1980) or Andrews & Pough (1985).

Also, is it something we should try and customise for our study species?

All the best,
Matt

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: QMET in ectotherms
parts:
Hi Matt,

It's based on the assumption that, to a rough approximation, 1 ml O2 consumed represents about 20 J energy. The equation referred to on those line you mentioned are for ml O2 / h and watts is J / s hence the conversion factor of 0.0056 for that particular equation to go from ml O2 / h to W.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: 与“QMET in ectotherms”相关的私人帖子
parts:
Hi Zhong-wen,

Good question. First, re the conversion, just to be clear, that paper I sent said about 3.4 cal / mg. There are about 1.43 mg / l O2 so the conversion from ml O2 / h to J / h is  3.4 * 1.4 * 4.186, i.e. about 20. To convert to watts (J/s) you then divide by 3600 to get 0.0056.

Re the differences you saw between Qmet and the outputted O2, that is because there are some caps on the allowable metabolic rate in the heat budget calculation - see code below. So the metabolic rate is not allowed to go to zero, but capped at 0.01 W, and when the animal is getting too hot it's capped at what it would be at 0.5 deg C above the VTmax.

When you put rain-limited activity on, it wasn't getting as hot. Hope that clears things up.

All the best,
Mike

       IF(TC .GT. 50)THEN
C       CAP METABOLIC RATE EQUATION WITH MAX OF TC = 50
        QMETAB = 0.0056*10.**(MR_3*50)*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
        GOTO 101
       ENDIF
       IF(TC.LE.TPREF)THEN
        IF(TC.GE.1.0)THEN
C        ACCEPTABLE TEMPERATURE RANGE
         QMETAB=0.0056*10.**(MR_3*TC)*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
        ELSE
         QMETAB = 0.01
        ENDIF
       ELSE
C       TOO HOT
C       ALLOWING TCORE TO BE A LITTLE HIGHER THAN TMAX PREFERRED SO THAT THERMOREGULATION
C       BEHAVIORS WILL BE INVOKED TO SELECT MORE MODERATE MICROCLIMATE CONDITIONS
        QMETAB = 0.0056*10.**(MR_3*(TMAXPR+0.5))*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
       ENDIF

Hi Zhong-wen,

I didn't totally follow your question. But, yes, I put it there so that you could simulate e.g. a frog that only comes out after rain. Turning it on may lead to higher body temperatures because it might be warmer in the retreat (underground) than out in the open. The rainact argument just adds an extra condition to activity, i.e. it has to be raining above the threshold amount on that day, the threshold being rainfall in mm. But, I also had code in the evaporation subroutine, SEVAP, to make humidity 99% when rainact was on and it was raining. I've just removed that code because it may not be a good assumption for some cases. It is better that you modify the metout/shadmet matrices manually to change humidity during rain events before passing them to the ectotherm model. That will also modify the body temperatures you get, because without the assumption of 99% RH, they may end up with lower body temperatures due to evaporative cooling.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Zhong-wen,

Good question. First, re the conversion, just to be clear, that paper I sent said about 3.4 cal / mg. There are about 1.43 mg / l O2 so the conversion from ml O2 / h to J / h is  3.4 * 1.4 * 4.186, i.e. about 20. To convert to watts (J/s) you then divide by 3600 to get 0.0056.

Re the differences you saw between Qmet and the outputted O2, that is because there are some caps on the allowable metabolic rate in the heat budget calculation - see code below. So the metabolic rate is not allowed to go to zero, but capped at 0.01 W, and when the animal is getting too hot it's capped at what it would be at 0.5 deg C above the VTmax.

When you put rain-limited activity on, it wasn't getting as hot. Hope that clears things up.

All the best,
Mike

       IF(TC .GT. 50)THEN
C       CAP METABOLIC RATE EQUATION WITH MAX OF TC = 50
        QMETAB = 0.0056*10.**(MR_3*50)*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
        GOTO 101
       ENDIF
       IF(TC.LE.TPREF)THEN
        IF(TC.GE.1.0)THEN
C        ACCEPTABLE TEMPERATURE RANGE
         QMETAB=0.0056*10.**(MR_3*TC)*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
        ELSE
         QMETAB = 0.01
        ENDIF
       ELSE
C       TOO HOT
C       ALLOWING TCORE TO BE A LITTLE HIGHER THAN TMAX PREFERRED SO THAT THERMOREGULATION
C       BEHAVIORS WILL BE INVOKED TO SELECT MORE MODERATE MICROCLIMATE CONDITIONS
        QMETAB = 0.0056*10.**(MR_3*(TMAXPR+0.5))*MR_1*GMASS**MR_2
       ENDIF
